epigraph: It waits in the dark between the stones.
vignette: The Umbral scribe stepped onto the cell. He did not shout. He pressed his hand to the wet ground. The soil turned black. It smelled of old iron. Dreadmaw rose from the mud. It had no eyes. It had only hunger. The Verdant archer loosed an arrow. The arrow hit the shadow and fell. The archer held his bow. He did not move. He knew the rule. One man could not kill this thing. The shadow grew thick. It pressed against the archer’s mind. He felt the weight of it. He looked at his companion. The companion looked back. They stood still. The ground under them grew cold. The Verdant line held because two men stood there. If one had fallen back the shadow would have taken the cell. It eats conviction. It waits for the lone wolf. The tower grew higher. The truth was heavy.
codex_note: Scholars note that Dreadmaw cannot be overwritten by a single opposing will, requiring coordinated conviction to suppress its inscribed terror.
